old-hands.door_fill: captor: a Night Market crew boss's men; why taken: leverage on the guild
old-hands.throughline: Because a Night Market crew boss wants revenge, he has his crew raid the crossings and caches and leave Old Hands seals behind for the watch, because years ago an Old Hands crossing-keeper gave his brother to the watch so that a house's load could pass; when the Old Hands struck first, over an old house that began buying from the Market, it was his answer: he sends his crew into the Old Gate House's own cellars, so the watch finds Old Hands seals there and the quarter is barred to the Old Hands for a night, then his men take the heart and hold her, and it comes to a head when the truce meeting ends with a poisoned cup, one dead on each side; the Market blames the heart's kin, and they must be got out of the Old Gate House before the reprisal.

faction_endings: make peace with the Old Hands
night-market.door_fill: blamed for holding back the take; taken by the Hand
night-market.throughline: Because an Old Hands steward wants more power, he has set the score everyone is whispering about as a trap, to break the Market and send its buyers back to the old houses; it is how the feud with the Night Market began, over an old house that began buying from the Market: he calls the Market out before the crews at a dockside card game, daring them to take the score, then you are framed for holding back the take, and it comes to a head when the truce meeting ends with a poisoned cup, one dead on each side, and the old don shields the killer.

holy-house.door_fill: cargo: the high priest, wounded; pursuer: a Last Wave raid leader's men
holy-house.throughline: Because a Last Wave raid leader wants revenge, he raids the wayside shrines and the towns that tithe to them, because the order's riders once burned his enclave's smoke hall as heathen; he cries in the markets that the house's shelter is worth nothing, then his men wound the high priest on the road, and it comes to a head when his raiders camp a night from the Mount, the tithe-towns' protection fails, and the heart's village is next.

faction_endings: let the showman run the show
dueling.door_fill: captor: a Banner Lord's master-at-arms, who gives the grand tournament's prize

blow_detail.how: taken in a fight by a lord

dueling.throughline: Because a Banner Lord's master-at-arms, who gives the grand tournament's prize, wants things kept as they are, he keeps giving the prize, a purse bound to a year's service in his lord's march, because the march is losing a feud and needs trained men, though that year has sent the ladder's last champions to die there; he takes the ladder's top fighter off it in front of the crowd, with the purse and its year of service, then fighters are pressed into his lord's guard by his men, and it comes to a head when his lord's muster calls up the ladder's top rungs under the prize's terms, and his men take the heart and the top rungs to serve them out.

lantern.door_fill: offended: whoever abandoning a comrade wronged
lantern.throughline: Because a hill-village headman whose son died when a Lantern chapter held his village for a lord wants revenge, he sends the Company false calls for help from the hill villages and turns the villages against any chapter that comes; he closes the caravan road to Lantern escorts with his men, then the heart is cried down for abandoning a comrade, and it comes to a head when his men take to the caravan road out of Carter's Rest as a band, and the caravan the heart rides with is the first they strike.

writers.door_fill: the stain: what the leader herself said of the player
writers.throughline: Because the leader herself wants things kept as they are, she has let every other copy of the region's land rolls go astray, so whoever holds the Writers decides who owns the land; she openly takes the lord's court rolls into her own keeping, so no other copyist touches them, then you are put down a rank on her word, and it comes to a head when she accuses the heart before the lord's court of a false copy of its rolls, and the halls' commission rides on the hearing.
